extracted.intended_audience: contributors and editors of the Wolfram Language Specification documentation (technical writers and developer contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for writing and formatting documentation and formal specification text for the Wolfram Language Specification repository (MkDocs/GitHub Markdown). Covers prose style, math typesetting, code examples, grammars, admonitions, authorship, and compatibility notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use GitHub Flavored Markdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Use GitHub Flavored Markdown (GFM) for article markup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The repository expects GFM; follow GFM semantics for code fences, inline code, math blocks, and other features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write in standard written English (Wikipedia Manual of Style approximation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Write in standard written English in approximation to Wikipedia's Manual of Style; maintain consistent style and formatting within an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "Style and formatting should be consistent within an article." Use Wikipedia's Manual of Style as a reference for choices where not otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special symbols: use entities or the character; prefer long names for private-use codepoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Almost every editor/browser can handle characters outside ASCII; use html entity, decimal reference, hex reference, or the character itself for special symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Mathematica/private-use codepoints (e.g. \[WolframLanguageLogo] which is a private-use codepoint), prefer the long name notation (e.g. \[WolframLanguageLogo]) because the codepoint may not be a valid Unicode character and may render as a placeholder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical typesetting: inline and display math conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline math is typeset between single $ signs; displayed math uses $$...$$ or \[...\].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: $\sqrt{1+x^2}$ for inline; $$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$$ or \[x=...\] for display. Important: a displayed math equation needs to be surrounded by newlines as if it were in its own paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code blocks: use fenced code blocks with explicit language identifier
rubrics_metrics.description: Place code within a fenced code block and include an explicit language identifier (e.g., ```wl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: ```wl StringJoin[Capitalize[ToLowerCase[StringSplit["my list"]]]] ``` Use the language specifier 'wl' (not 'mma' or 'mathematica'). See Pygments docs for other specifiers (python, c, cpp, latex, perl, antlr, java, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inline code: use backticks and keep inline code short
rubrics_metrics.description: Set off inline code with backticks (`), optionally with an inline language specifier; only short pieces of code should be inlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: `#!wl f[N@{g/@m}]` renders as f[N@{g/@m}]. Short fragments like `PrimeQ/@Range[20]` are acceptable; longer definitions (multi-line functions) are too long to inline and should be in code fences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'wl' as the language identifier for Wolfram Language code
rubrics_metrics.description: When specifying the language for WL code blocks, use 'wl' as the identifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use 'mma' or 'mathematica' as the language identifier for WL code blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: GFM does not word-wrap WL code: break long lines and indent continuations
rubrics_metrics.description: Because GFM does not word-wrap WL code blocks, add line breaks for long lines and indent continuations to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indent continuation lines to show they are continuations of the same expression and avoid horizontal scrollbars in rendered docs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish input from output using In/Out labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish input expressions from output expressions using the In[1]:= and Out[2]= labels as in the Mathematica command-line interface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example formatting: In[1]:= expr ... Out[1]= "MyList". As an alternative, placing the expected output immediately below the expression in a code comment is acceptable (e.g., (* "MyList" *)), though this loses output syntax highlighting. Use InputForm where helpful to clarify the form of outputs (e.g., quoted strings).

rubrics_metrics.name: When writing WL specifications, flag compatibility issues with Mathematica
rubrics_metrics.description: Always make note of where there can be incompatibilities with Mathematica by using a 'Compatibility Warning' admonition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the admonition syntax and the 'Compatibility Warning' title to explicitly call out incompatibilities between WL spec and Mathematica behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal grammars should be treated as pseudocode unless explicitly labeled
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal grammar representations are considered pseudocode unless explicitly labelled as a specific grammar syntax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express grammars in common Flex/Bison syntax while allowing regular expressions within productions; lexical rules may be capitalized by tradition; end productions with a semicolon. When using ANTLR4 conventions, mark nested-only productions as 'fragment' to indicate they cannot appear standalone. If a pure Bison/Flex/ANTLR4 or pure regex is intended, label it with the specific grammar or regex syntax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Label the grammar/regex syntax standard when using specific features
rubrics_metrics.description: When you use features specific to a particular grammar or regex standard (e.g., PCRE, POSIX, Perl), explicitly indicate that syntax standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids ambiguity about portability and intended parser behavior when readers copy grammar or regex examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admonitions: use the Admonitions plugin and allowed environments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Admonitions plugin for MkDocs to present warnings, tips, examples, etc., and use the documented admonition environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available admonitions: Important, Abstract, Info, Tip, Success, Question, Warning, Failure, Danger, Bug, Example, Quote. Syntax example: !!! warning "Compatibility Warning" followed by indented content. Admonitions render with a title and body as shown in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and bylines
rubrics_metrics.description: Bylines are optional; if you add significant content to an article that already has a byline, feel free to add your name to the byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither adding a byline nor leaving one is required; use judgment about attribution for significant contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: WL code readability: favor whitespace and readable layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Whitespace and readable indentation improve WL code readability; prefer clear indentation and breaks rather than dense single-line expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the guide show adding line breaks and indentation to make nested function calls and argument lists easier to scan. Even small amounts of whitespace can make a big difference.
